title: The New Mission
paragraphs: §Jesus Goes Up

Yo Theophilus, what's up? In my first book, I told you all about what Jesus did and taught, right up until he peaced out and went to heaven. After he came back from the dead, he hung out with his chosen apostles for 40 days, proving he was for real. They just chilled, and he told them all about God's kingdom.

One time, while they were eating, he gave them a direct order: "Don't leave Jerusalem. Wait for the special gift my Father promised, the one I told you about. John the Baptist just used water, but you guys are about to get a major upgrade with the Holy Spirit, and it's coming soon."

So, when they were all together for the last time, they asked him, "Hey, boss, is it time? Are you gonna make Israel the top dog again now?" Jesus was like, "Chill, the timing is my Father's business, not yours. But here's what you *do* get: the Holy Spirit. When he comes, you'll get this insane power to be my witnesses. You'll start in Jerusalem, then go all over Judea and Samaria, and then, like, to the whole world."

Right after he said that, he started floating up into the sky and disappeared into a cloud. They were all just standing there, staring up, totally stunned. Suddenly, two guys in bright white clothes appeared next to them and said, "You guys from Galilee, why are you just staring at the sky? This same Jesus, who was just taken from you into heaven, is going to come back in the exact same way you saw him go."

After that, the crew walked back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, which was like a short walk. They went straight to the upstairs room where they were staying. The whole squad was there: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James (the son of Alphaeus), Simon the Zealot, and Judas (the son of James).
They were all on the same page, spending all their time praying together. The women were there too, along with Jesus's mom, Mary, and his brothers. They were all in.

After a few days, Peter stood up in front of the whole group, about 120 people, and said, "Listen up, everyone. The prophecy from the Holy Spirit, spoken by King David, had to come true. It was about Judas, the guy who betrayed Jesus and led the temple guards to arrest him. He was one of us, part of the team.

(Here's the dirt on Judas: he took the bribe money and bought a field. But then he had a gnarly fall, his stomach burst open, and all his guts spilled out. Everyone in Jerusalem heard about it, and they even named the field 'Field of Blood.')

"It's written in the book of Psalms: 'Let his place be empty; let no one live there,' and also, 'Let someone else take his job.' So now we have to pick a replacement for Judas. It has to be one of the guys who was with us the whole time, from when Jesus was baptized by John until the day he was taken up to heaven. This new guy will be a witness with us that Jesus rose from the dead."

They nominated two guys: Joseph, who was also called Barsabbas (and nicknamed Justus), and Matthias. Then they prayed, "God, you know everyone's heart. Show us which of these two you've chosen to take over this ministry and leadership role that Judas ditched to go to his own place." Then they drew straws, and the lot fell to Matthias. So he was officially added to the eleven apostles, making them a solid twelve again.

title: The Holy Spirit Drops In
paragraphs: §The Holy Spirit Drops

So, all the disciples were chilling together for the Pentecost holiday. Suddenly, this crazy-loud wind rips through the house out of nowhere. Then, BAM! The Holy Spirit shows up like a boss, and they all start talking in different languages, and flames like tongues of fire appeared above each of them, like they suddenly knew every language or something. It was an amazing change for the whole squad.

A huge crowd of people from all over the world were in town. When they heard the noise, they came running. They were totally buggin' out because they heard these guys from Galilee speaking their own languages perfectly. They said, "Listen, how is this even possible?" Some of them were amazed, but the haters said, "Psh, they're just drunk."

Then Peter, the leader of the disciples, stood up and was like, "Listen up, people! These guys aren't drunk. It's only 9 in the morning! This is what the prophet Joel was talking about. God is pouring out his Spirit on everyone. Your sons and daughters will have the inside scoop, your young men will have visions, and your old men will have epic dreams."
§Peter's First Sermon

Peter went on to say, "You all know about Jesus, the guy who did all those miracles. You let him get captured and killed, but God flexed his power and brought him back to life. King David even wrote about it, saying that God wouldn't let his Holy One rot in the grave. We're all witnesses! Jesus is alive, and he's the one who sent the Holy Spirit you're seeing and hearing right now. So, let's be real, you messed up big time. You killed the Messiah! God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah."

The crowd was stunned. They asked Peter, "Look, what do we do now?" Peter told them, "You need to change your lives, turn to God, and get baptized in the name of Jesus. Then your sins will be forgiven, and you'll get the gift of the Holy Spirit too. This promise is for you, your kids, and everyone else God invites."

That day, about 3,000 people joined the Jesus fan club. They were all about learning from the apostles, hanging out together, sharing meals, and praying. It was the most awesome community, living in pure harmony. They even sold their stuff and shared the money with anyone who needed it. They were all in, and God kept adding more and more people to their crew every day.

title: Lame Dude Gets a Miraculous Healing
paragraphs: §Healing at the Temple Gate

So, Peter and John were heading to the Temple for a prayer sesh around 3 PM. Right at the "Beautiful" gate, they see this guy who's been crippled since day one, basically just chilling there, asking for cash from everyone going in. He spots Peter and John and is like, "Hey, spare some change?" Peter, with John right there, locks eyes with the man and says, "Hey, look at us." The guy looks up, probably thinking he's about to get some serious coin.

But Peter hits him with, "Look, I'm broke. I don't have any money. But what I *do* have, I'll give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!" Then he grabs the guy's hand and yanks him up. Instantly, the man's feet and ankles get super strong. He literally jumps up and starts walking. An absolute miracle.

The guy, totally stoked, goes into the Temple with them, just walking around, dancing, and shouting out how awesome God is. Everyone there sees him and is like, "Wait, isn't that the guy who's always begging at the gate?" They were all bugging out, totally shocked at what they were seeing.
The man was so excited he was hugging Peter and John, and a massive crowd ran over to Solomon's Porch to see what was up.
§Peter Explains

When Peter saw he had an audience, he went off. "Hey, people of Israel, why are you so surprised? And why are you staring at us like *we* did this with our own power? The God of our ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, just showed his power and glorified His Son Jesus. This is the same Jesus you guys ghosted and told Pilate to get rid of, even when Pilate said He was innocent. You dissed the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be freed instead. You literally took out the Author of Life, but God brought him back from the dead, and we're the receipts. It was faith in Jesus' name that healed this guy you all know. Straight up, faith in Jesus made him 100% better, right in front of you.

"Look, bros, I know you and your leaders had no clue what you were really doing when you messed up and had Jesus killed. But God knew. He used your epic fail to make what the prophets had been saying all along come true—that the Messiah had to suffer. So now you gotta switch it up! Turn back to God, so He can wipe your slate clean and send some major blessings your way. He'll send Jesus, the Messiah He's got lined up for you. But for now, Jesus is chilling in heaven until it's time to restore everything, just like God's been saying through his prophets since way back. Even Moses said, 'God's gonna send a prophet just like me from your own people. You better listen to every single thing he says, or you'll be totally cut off.'

"All the prophets, from Samuel on, were all talking about these days. You guys are the heirs of those prophets and the deal God made with your ancestors. Remember what God told Abraham? 'Through your family, everyone on earth will be blessed.' And you're first in line for that blessing. God raised up His Son and sent him to you first, to bless you by helping you turn away from your messed-up lives."

title: The Apostles Get Grounded
paragraphs: §Arrested for Preaching

So, Peter and John were talking to a huge crowd when a bunch of priests, the head of the temple cops, and some super-religious leaders called Sadducees showed up furious. They were totally furious that Peter and John were telling everyone that Jesus had risen from the dead. So, they arrested them and threw them in jail for the night. But here's the thing, about five thousand people who heard the message said, "Whoa, this is legit," and started believing.

The next day, all the important leaders in Jerusalem had a meeting. We're talking rulers, religious leaders, the brainy scholars, the head priest Annas, Caiaphas, John, Alexander—the whole group of religious leaders was there. They dragged Peter and John into the middle of the room and started grilling them, asking, "Who gave you the right to do any of this?"

But Peter, totally powered up by the Holy Spirit, just roasts them. "Hey, leaders! If we're on trial for helping a sick guy, let me be straight up with you—we've got nothing to hide. This was all done in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, the guy you killed, but God brought back to life. He's the reason this man is standing here totally fine. You builders threw Jesus out like trash, but now he's the cornerstone of everything. There's no other way to be saved, no other name that matters. Only Jesus."
§Told to Shut Up

The leaders were stunned. Peter and John were just ordinary guys with no fancy degrees, but they were so confident. Then they realized—these guys were part of Jesus's crew. And with the healed man standing right there, they were totally speechless. What could they even say?

They sent Peter and John out of the room to come up with a plan. "What are we gonna do with these guys?" they whispered. "Everyone in town knows they did a miracle. We can't deny it. But we gotta shut this down before it spreads. Let's threaten them and tell them to never talk about Jesus again."

So they called Peter and John back in and told them to stop talking about Jesus. But Peter and John said, "You tell us what's right: listening to you or listening to God? We can't just ghost what we've seen and heard." The leaders threatened them some more but had to let them go because they couldn't find a reason to keep them in jail. The people were all praising God for what happened, and the man who was healed was over forty years old!

As soon as they were free, Peter and John went back to their friends and told them everything. When their friends heard the story, they all prayed together, "God, you're the one who made everything. You spoke through our ancestor David, who said that the world's leaders would team up against you and your Messiah. And that's exactly what happened! Herod, Pontius Pilate, and all the people plotted against your holy Son, Jesus. But they were just playing into your hands and your plan all along. So now, check out their threats and give us the guts to keep preaching your message. Flex your power with healings and miracles in the name of Jesus."
§The Believers Share Everything
While they were praying, the whole house started shaking. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and kept speaking God's word without any fear.

All the believers were like one big family—they shared everything. No one was selfish and said, "That's mine." They even sold their houses and land and gave the money to the apostles to share with anyone who needed it. One guy, Joseph, who the apostles called Barnabas (which means "the encourager"), a Levite from Cyprus, sold a field he owned and gave all the money to the apostles. What a bro.

title: The Ultimate Lie Detector Test
paragraphs: §Ananias and Sapphira

So, there was this guy Ananias and his wife, Sapphira. They sold a piece of land, but then they got this dishonest scheme. They decided to keep some of the cash for themselves and only give the rest to the apostles, acting like they were giving the full amount. Complete deception.

Peter wasn't having it. He was like, “Ananias, my guy, why’d you let Satan talk you into lying to the Holy Spirit? You think you can hold out on God? Before you sold the land, it was yours. After you sold it, the money was yours. So why pull a stunt like this? You didn’t just lie to us; you straight-up lied to God.”

As soon as Peter said that, Ananias just dropped dead on the spot. And everyone who heard about it was totally freaked out. Some of the younger guys came, wrapped him up, and hauled him out to be buried.
About three hours later, his wife Sapphira came in, not knowing what had happened to her husband. Peter asked her, “So, tell me, was this the full price you got for the field?”
§More Miracles and More Trouble
She said, “Yep, that’s the price.”

Peter was like, “Wow. So you two were in on this together, conspiring against the Spirit of the Master? The guys who just buried your husband are at the door, and guess what? You’re next.” And boom, she fell down dead too. The young men came back, found her, and buried her right next to her husband.
After that, the whole church and everyone else who heard the story had a major reality check. They knew God wasn't someone you could just mess with.

Meanwhile, the apostles were out there flexing their God-given powers, doing all sorts of amazing miracles and signs. They would all hang out together at the Temple on Solomon’s Porch, in total harmony. People thought they were awesome, but nobody from the outside dared to join them. Still, more and more people, both men and women, started believing in the Master and joining the crew.

It got so crazy that people would bring their sick friends and family out into the streets, laying them on mats and beds, just hoping that Peter’s shadow might fall on them as he walked by. Crowds of people came from all the towns around Jerusalem, bringing their sick and those who were tormented by evil spirits. And every single one of them was healed.

But the high priest and his crew, the Sadducees, got super salty about all this. They were so jealous that they had the apostles arrested and thrown in the public jail. But that night, an angel of the Lord came, opened the jail doors, and led them out. The angel said, “Go back to the Temple and tell the people everything about this new life.”
So, at the crack of dawn, they went right back to the Temple and started teaching again.

Later that morning, the high priest and his cronies got the whole High Council together and sent for the prisoners. But when the guards got to the jail, the apostles were gone. They went back and reported, “The jail was locked up tight, and the guards were at their posts, but when we opened the doors, there was nobody inside.”
The captain of the Temple guard and the chief priests were totally baffled. They were like, “What in the world is going on?”

Then someone ran in and said, “You’re not gonna believe this, but the men you put in jail are back in the Temple, teaching the people!” So the captain and his guards went and got them. They were gentle this time because they were afraid the people would riot.

They brought the apostles before the High Council, and the high priest started grilling them. “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this Jesus’ name, right? And what do you do? You fill all of Jerusalem with your teaching and try to blame us for this man’s death!”

Peter and the other apostles just looked at them and said, “We have to obey God, not you. The God of our ancestors raised Jesus from the dead—the same Jesus you killed by hanging him on a cross. God has put him in the place of honor, as our Prince and Savior, to give Israel a chance to change their lives and be forgiven of their sins. We are witnesses to all of this, and so is the Holy Spirit, who God gives to everyone who obeys him.”

When the council heard that, they were furious and wanted to kill the apostles right then and there. But one of them, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, who was a respected teacher of the law, stood up. He had the apostles taken out of the room for a minute and then said to the council, “Men of Israel, be careful what you’re about to do to these men. Remember that guy Theudas who showed up a while ago, claiming to be a big shot? He got about four hundred followers, but then he was killed, and his whole movement fell apart. Then there was Judas the Galilean, who got a following during the census. He died too, and his followers scattered.

“So here’s my advice: leave these men alone. If what they’re doing is just a human thing, it will fail. But if it’s from God, you won’t be able to stop them. You might even find yourselves fighting against God.”
They all thought that was pretty solid advice. So they called the apostles back in, had them whipped, and warned them again not to speak in the name of Jesus. Then they let them go.

The apostles left the High Council, not bummed out, but overjoyed that they were considered worthy to be dishonored for the name of Jesus. And they didn’t stop for a second. Every single day, in the Temple and in people’s homes, they kept on teaching and preaching the good news that Jesus is the Christ.

title: The Food Fight and the First A-Team
paragraphs: §The Seven Chosen

So, the church was blowing up, and new people were joining left and right. But with more people came more problems. The Greek-speaking crew started beefing with the Hebrew-speaking crew because their widows were getting ghosted during the daily food handouts. It was a total mess.

The Twelve apostles, the OG leaders, called a big meeting. They said, "Hey, it's not cool for us to stop preaching and teaching God's Word just to manage food distribution. So, here's the plan: pick seven men from your crew who everyone trusts, who are full of the Holy Spirit and have some common sense, and we'll put them in charge of the food. That way, we can stick to our main calling: praying and spreading the Word."

The whole crew thought this was a brilliant idea. They picked seven men: Stephen (a man with major faith and Holy Spirit power), Philip, Procorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas. They brought them to the apostles, who prayed, laid hands on them, and officially made them the first team for handling business.
§Stephen Shines
And you know what? It worked. The Word of God kept spreading, and the number of followers in Jerusalem went through the roof. Even a bunch of priests got on board.

Meanwhile, Stephen was experiencing a life-changing moment. He was full of God's grace and energy, doing insane miracles and flexing his power. But some haters from a group of freed slaves, and guys from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia, tried to start an argument with him. They were no match for his wisdom and the Spirit he spoke with. He totally roasted them.
§Stephen Gets Arrested

So, they decided to play dirty. They secretly paid off some guys to lie and say, "We heard him cursing Moses and God!" That got everyone riled up—the regular folks, the religious leaders, and the Bible experts. They grabbed Stephen and dragged him in front of the High Council, the religious leaders and Bible experts.

Then they brought in their paid-off witnesses, who said, "This guy never shuts up about how much he hates this holy place and God's Law. We even heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth is going to tear this place down and cancel all the traditions Moses gave us."
But as everyone on the High Council stared at Stephen, they saw something wild. His face looked like the face of an angel. Straight up.

title: Stephen's Mic Drop
paragraphs: §Stephen's Speech
Then the head priest was like, “So, what’s your deal? You got something to say for yourself?”

Stephen, totally chill, was like, “Aight, listen up, my guys and dads. God, in all his glory, showed up to our great-great-great-grandpappy Abraham way back when he was in Mesopotamia, even before he bounced to Haran. God told him, ‘Hey, leave your fam and your country. I’m gonna show you a new place.’
§God's Promise to Abraham

So Abraham peaced out of the Chaldees and rolled into Haran. After his dad died, he moved to this land where we’re all living now. But God didn’t give him any of it, not even a tiny piece of land to his name. But he promised to give the whole country to him and his kid later, even though Abraham didn’t even have a kid yet. God also gave him a heads-up that his descendants would be foreigners in another country, and they’d be enslaved and treated like dirt for 400 years. But God was like, ‘Don’t trip, I’ll handle those slave owners and get my people out so they can worship me here.’

Then God made a deal with Abraham, like a bro-pact, and sealed it with circumcision. When Abraham had his son, Isaac, he did the same thing to him. Isaac had Jacob, and Jacob had the twelve OGs, the founding fathers of our tribes, and they all kept the tradition going.

But then those “fathers” got super jelly of their brother Joseph and sold him as a slave to Egypt. But God had his back. He saved him from all his problems and even made him tight with Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Pharaoh was so impressed with Joseph that he basically made him the ruler of the whole country, even his own house.

Then a massive famine hit the whole area, from Egypt to Canaan, and it was brutal. Our ancestors were starving and couldn’t find any food. Jacob heard there was food in Egypt, so he sent our ancestors to check it out. They confirmed it and went back a second time to get more. That’s when Joseph told them who he really was and introduced his whole family to Pharaoh. Then Joseph sent for his dad, Jacob, and the whole fam, 75 people in total. And that’s how we all ended up in Egypt.
Jacob and our ancestors died there, and they were buried in the tomb that Abraham bought from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.

When the 400 years were almost up, the time God promised to save our people, our population in Egypt was huge. Then a new king who didn’t know Joseph came to power. He was totally cruel to our people and made us leave our newborn babies outside to die. It was messed up.

Right around then, Moses was born, and he was a super cute baby. His parents hid him for three months, but when they couldn’t hide him anymore, they put him outside. Pharaoh’s daughter found him and raised him like her own son. Moses went to the best schools in Egypt and became powerful in both words and actions.

When Moses was 40, he wanted to see how his Hebrew bros were doing, so he went to check on them. He saw an Egyptian beating up one of his people, so he stepped in and knocked the Egyptian out. He thought his people would be stoked that he was on their side and that God was using him to save them. But they weren’t. The next day, two of them were fighting, and he tried to break it up, telling them to be cool with each other. He was like, ‘Guys, you’re brothers, why are you fighting?’

But the guy who started the fight was like, ‘Who made you our boss? You gonna kill me like you killed that Egyptian yesterday?’ When Moses heard that, he knew he was in deep trouble, so he bounced to Midian and lived there as a foreigner. He had two sons while he was there.

Forty years later, in the middle of nowhere at Mount Sinai, an angel appeared to him in a burning bush. Moses couldn’t believe his eyes, so he went to get a closer look. Then he heard God’s voice, ‘I’m the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses was so scared he couldn’t even look.
God said, ‘Take off your shoes, you’re on holy ground. I’ve seen how much my people are suffering in Egypt. I’ve heard them crying, and I’m here to help. So get ready, I’m sending you back to Egypt.’

This is the same Moses they had dissed earlier, saying, ‘Who made you our boss?’ But God sent him back as their leader and savior, with the help of the angel in the burning bush. He led them out of slavery and did all sorts of crazy miracles in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the desert for 40 years. This is the same Moses who told our people, ‘God will send you a prophet just like me from your own people.’ This is the Moses who was the middleman between the angel at Mount Sinai and our ancestors in the desert. He got the life-giving words from God and gave them to us, but our ancestors wanted nothing to do with them.

They missed the old days in Egypt and whined to Aaron, ‘Make us some gods we can see and follow. We don’t know what happened to this Moses guy who brought us out here.’ That’s when they made a golden calf, worshiped it, and threw a party for themselves for their awesome new religion.

God was not happy. He let them do their own thing and worship whatever they wanted, but they had to deal with the consequences. The prophet Amos wrote about it: ‘Did you really bring me sacrifices during those 40 years in the desert, Israel? Nah. You were too busy building shrines to your fake gods. That’s why I sent you into exile in Babylon.’

And the whole time, our ancestors had a portable tent for worshiping the real God, made exactly how God told Moses to make it. They had it with them when they followed Joshua and took over the land from the pagans, and they had it all the way down to King David. David wanted to build a permanent house for God, but Solomon was the one who actually built it.

But that doesn’t mean God lives in a house made by people. The prophet Isaiah said it best: ‘Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. So what kind of house are you gonna build for me? Where can I chill and relax? I already built everything.’

And you guys are just as stubborn as your ancestors! You’re deaf and blind to the Holy Spirit. You’re just like them. Was there ever a prophet your ancestors didn’t persecute? They killed anyone who even talked about the coming of the Righteous One. And you’ve kept up the family tradition—you’re all traitors and murderers. You got God’s law delivered by angels, gift-wrapped, and you totally blew it!”
§Stephen Is Killed

When they heard that, they went totally ballistic. They were screaming and yelling and throwing a fit. But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, didn’t even notice. He was just looking at God in all his glory, with Jesus standing right next to him. He said, “Whoa! I see heaven wide open and the Son of Man standing next to God!”

They all started yelling and covering their ears and rushed him. They dragged him out of the city and started throwing rocks at him. The guys who started it all took off their coats and had a young guy named Saul watch them.
As they were stoning him, Stephen prayed, “Jesus, take my life.” Then he knelt down and yelled, “Master, don’t hold this against them.” And with that, he died.
And Saul was right there, approving of the killing.

title: The Magician and the Road Trip
paragraphs: §The Church Scatters

So, after Stephen's crazy death, things got real for the church in Jerusalem. A man named Saul basically went on a rampage against the church, going house to house and dragging Jesus's followers to jail. It was a total mess. Because of the heat, all the believers, except for the main apostles, scattered and left town.

But here's the cool part: as they scattered, they started spreading the word about Jesus everywhere they went. They were like secret agents for God. One of the guys, Philip, went down to a city in Samaria. He started telling everyone about Jesus, and people were hooked. He was doing all these miracles, healing people who couldn't walk, and casting out demons who were screaming as they left. The whole city was buzzing with excitement.

Now, before Philip got there, this city had a local celebrity: a magician named Simon. This guy had everyone fooled. He did all these flashy tricks and people thought he had some kind of superpower. They called him "The Great One." But when Philip showed up with the real power of God, Simon suddenly looked like a cheap knock-off. Everyone, including Simon, believed in Jesus and got baptized. Simon was so blown away that he started following Philip everywhere, like a superfan, amazed by the real miracles.

Back in Jerusalem, the head apostles heard that Samaria was getting into Jesus, so they sent Peter and John to check it out. When they got there, they realized the new believers had been baptized, but they hadn't received the Holy Spirit yet. So, Peter and John laid their hands on them, and BAM, they received the Holy Spirit. It was like a spiritual transformation.

Simon the magician saw this and his jaw dropped. He saw this incredible power being given just by a touch and immediately wanted in. He pulled out his wallet and said to Peter and John, "Hey, how much for that power? I'll pay whatever you want. Just show me the trick!"
§Simon's Big Mistake

Peter was not having it. He totally roasted Simon. "To heck with you and your money! You think you can buy a gift from God? You are so out of line. You're all twisted up inside with greed. You better pray to God and hope he forgives you for thinking something so messed up." Simon got super scared and begged them, "Oh man, please pray for me! Pray that I don't get wrecked for this!"
After that, Peter and John headed back to Jerusalem, but they preached in a bunch of other Samaritan towns on the way.
§Philip and the Ethiopian

Then, an angel of God gave Philip a new mission. "Hey, go south to that desert road that goes from Jerusalem to Gaza." So Philip just went. On the road, he saw a super important guy from Ethiopia. This guy was the treasurer for the queen of Ethiopia, basically the important official in charge of all the money. He was riding in his fancy chariot, reading the book of Isaiah.
The Holy Spirit told Philip, "Go catch up to that chariot." Philip ran up and heard the guy reading. He asked him, "Hey, do you get what you're reading?"

The Ethiopian guy was like, "How can I? I need someone to explain it to me." He invited Philip to hop in the chariot with him. The part he was reading was about a sheep being led to be slaughtered, who didn't make a sound. It was about someone who was treated unfairly and then taken from the earth.
"So," the Ethiopian asked, "is the prophet talking about himself, or someone else?" This was the perfect opening. Philip started with that exact verse and told him all about Jesus.

As they were riding, they passed some water. The Ethiopian said, "Look, water! What's stopping me from getting baptized right now?" He ordered the chariot to stop, and they both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him. When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of God suddenly teleported Philip away. The Ethiopian never saw him again, but he didn't even care. He was so happy because he had found what he was looking for. He went on his way, totally joyful.
Philip reappeared in another town called Azotus and kept on traveling, telling everyone the good news about Jesus in all the towns until he got to Caesarea.

title: The Ultimate Transformation
paragraphs: §Saul Meets Jesus

Meanwhile, this guy Saul was still on a rampage, basically a one-man wrecking crew against anyone who followed Jesus. He went to the head priest and got a warrant to go to Damascus. His plan? Find any of Jesus' followers, guys or girls, and drag them back to Jerusalem.

So he's on the road, almost at Damascus, when BAM! A super bright light from the sky flashes all around him. He falls to the ground and hears a voice, "Saul, Saul, why are you trying to take me down?"
Saul, completely stunned, asks, "Who are you, sir?"
The voice answers, "I'm Jesus. The one you're hunting. Now get up, go into the city, and you'll be told what to do next."

Saul's buddies just stood there, speechless. They heard the voice but didn't see anyone. When Saul got up, he was completely blind. They had to lead him by the hand into Damascus. For three days, he couldn't see a thing and didn't eat or drink anything.
Now, in Damascus, there was a follower of Jesus named Ananias. Jesus spoke to him in a vision, "Ananias."
"Yeah, Lord?" he answered.

"Get up and go to the street called Straight. At Judas's house, ask for a guy from Tarsus named Saul. He's praying right now. He just had a vision that a man named Ananias would come and lay hands on him so he could see again."

Ananias was like, "Uh, Lord, are you serious? I've heard all about this guy and the terrible things he's done to your people in Jerusalem. He's here with a warrant from the head priests to arrest all of us!"

But Jesus told him, "Don't worry. Go. I've chosen him to be my chosen instrument, to represent me to everyone—people who aren't Jews, kings, and even the Jews themselves. And I'm going to show him how much he's going to have to go through for me."

So Ananias went, found the house, and laid his hands on Saul. "Brother Saul," he said, "the Lord Jesus, the one you saw on the road, sent me so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit." Instantly, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see! He got up, was baptized, and then they all had a big meal together.
§Saul Starts Preaching

Saul hung out with the disciples in Damascus for a few days, and then he got right to it. He went to the synagogues and started telling everyone that Jesus is the Son of God. People were shocked. "Isn't this the guy who was trying to destroy the believers in Jerusalem?" they said. "Didn't he come here to arrest them and take them to the head priests?"

But Saul just got more and more powerful. He completely out-argued the Jews in Damascus, proving to them that Jesus is the Messiah. After a while, some of them got so mad they plotted to kill him. But Saul found out about their plan. They were watching the city gates 24/7 to catch him. So one night, his new friends helped him escape by lowering him in a basket over the city wall.

When Saul got back to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all scared of him. They didn't believe he was really a follower now. But then a guy named Barnabas took him under his wing and introduced him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen Jesus on the road and how he had boldly preached in Jesus' name in Damascus.

After that, they finally accepted him. He went all over Jerusalem with them, preaching fearlessly in the name of the Lord. He even got into some heated debates with some Greek-speaking Jews, who then started plotting to kill him. When the believers found out, they snuck him out of the city to Caesarea and then sent him off to his hometown of Tarsus.

With Saul gone, things finally chilled out for the church. All over Judea, Galilee, and Samaria, the church grew and got stronger. They had a deep respect for God, and the Holy Spirit was with them, making them prosper.

In the meantime, Peter was traveling around, visiting all the believers. In Lydda, he met a man named Aeneas who had been paralyzed and stuck in bed for eight years. Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed." And just like that, he jumped up.
Everyone in Lydda and Sharon saw him walking around and realized that God was for real.

In the nearby town of Joppa, there was a disciple named Tabitha, which means "Gazelle." She was famous for all the good things she did and for helping the poor. While Peter was in the area, she got sick and died. Her friends washed her body and laid her in an upstairs room.

When the disciples in Joppa heard that Peter was in Lydda, they sent two men to beg him to come right away. Peter went with them, and when he got there, they took him to the room where Tabitha's body was. All her friends, mostly widows, were crying and showing Peter the clothes she had made for them.

Peter made everyone leave the room. He knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up. He took her hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called everyone back in and showed them that she was alive.
The news spread like wildfire all over Joppa, and many people started believing in the Lord. Peter stayed in Joppa for a while, crashing at the house of a guy named Simon, who was a tanner.

title: God's Got No Faves
paragraphs: §Peter's Vision

So there's this guy, Cornelius. He's a captain in the Roman army, stationed in a town called Caesarea. Not just any captain, but the head of the Italian Guard. Basically, a pretty important guy. But he's not a bully about it. He's a good guy, and he and his whole family are all about God. He's always giving to the poor and praying.
One afternoon, around 3 PM, he's just chilling and praying when, bam, an angel shows up. Like, a legit angel, right there in his room. The angel says, "Cornelius."
Cornelius is totally bugging out. He's staring at the angel and is like, "Uh, what's up, sir?"

The angel tells him, "God's heard your prayers and seen you helping people. He's totally noticed you. So here's the deal: send some guys to Joppa to find a man named Simon, who everyone calls Peter. He's staying with another Simon, a tanner, who lives by the sea."
As soon as the angel ghosts him, Cornelius calls two of his servants and a soldier he trusts, a real devout guy. He tells them everything that just went down and sends them off to Joppa.

The next day, while the three guys are getting close to Joppa, Peter goes up to the roof to pray. It's about noon, and he's getting hungry. While he's waiting for lunch, he goes into a trance. He sees the sky open up and this giant blanket thing being lowered by its four corners. On the blanket are all kinds of animals—like, every animal you can think of, even the ones that are totally not kosher. Then a voice says, "Go for it, Peter. Kill it and eat it."
Peter's like, "No way, Lord! I've never eaten anything that's not kosher in my life."
The voice comes back a second time, "If God says it's cool, it's cool." This happens three times, and then the blanket is yanked back up into the sky.

Peter is super confused. He's trying to figure out what the heck that was all about when Cornelius's guys show up at the front door. They ask if a Simon, also known as Peter, is staying there. Peter's so deep in thought he doesn't even hear them. So the Holy Spirit whispers to him, "Hey, three guys are at the door looking for you. Go down and go with them. Don't even ask why. I sent them."
So Peter goes downstairs and says, "I'm your guy. What's up?"

They tell him, "Our boss, Captain Cornelius, is a super respected guy who loves God. An angel told him to invite you to his house so he could hear what you have to say." Peter invites them in for the night.

The next morning, Peter and some of his friends from Joppa head out with Cornelius's men. When they get to Caesarea, Cornelius is waiting with all his relatives and close friends. As soon as Peter walks in, Cornelius falls at his feet to worship him. But Peter pulls him up and says, "Whoa, guy, get up. I'm just a man, like you."

They go inside, and Peter sees the whole crew. He says, "You guys know this is weird, right? Jews don't hang out with non-Jews. But God just showed me that he doesn't play favorites. No one is 'unclean.' So when you sent for me, I came right away. So, for real, why'd you send for me?"

Cornelius explains the whole angel story. "Four days ago, I was praying, and this crazy bright guy showed up and told me to send for you. So I did. And you came. That's awesome. Now we're all here, ready to hear whatever God wants you to tell us."

Peter is so stoked. He's like, "Whoa, this is for real! God doesn't have a favorites list. It doesn't matter who you are or where you're from. If you're into God and do what's right, you're in. He sent a message to the people of Israel, and that message is that through Jesus, everything is getting put back together. And he's not just doing it for the Jews; he's doing it for everyone."

"You know the story. It started in Galilee after John the Baptist was telling everyone to change their lives. Then Jesus from Nazareth showed up, and God flexed his power and gave him the Holy Spirit. Jesus went all over the place, helping people and healing everyone who was getting took down by the devil. He could do all this because God was with him."

"And we saw it all. Everything he did. And then they killed him, hung him on a cross. But three days later, God brought him back to life. Not everyone saw him, just the witnesses God hand-picked, which was us! We ate and drank with him after he came back from the dead. He told us to tell everyone that he's the one God chose to be the judge of everyone, living and dead. And it's not just us saying it. All the prophets said that anyone who believes in him will have their sins forgiven."

While Peter is still talking, the Holy Spirit comes down on everyone listening. The Jewish believers who came with Peter are totally shocked. They can't believe the Holy Spirit is being given to non-Jews. But then they hear them speaking in other languages and praising God.

Peter's like, "Well, I guess that settles it. Anyone got a problem with baptizing these guys? They got the Holy Spirit, just like we did." No one said a word. So he ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to hang out for a few more days.

title: God Shows No Favorites
paragraphs: §Peter Explains

The news that Peter was hanging with non-Jews went viral. The head honchos in Jerusalem heard that a bunch of outsiders were suddenly part of the crew. When Peter showed up, his old squad, the "Circumcision Crew," totally called him out. They said, "Listen, what's the deal? You're chilling with those guys, eating their non-kosher food? You're messing up our whole brand!"

Peter was like, "Alright, chill. Let me break it down for you." He told them, "I was in Joppa, just praying, when I zoned out and had this crazy vision. A giant picnic blanket floated down from the sky. On it was a whole zoo—farm animals, wild beasts, crawling creatures, birds, everything. I was just staring at it, totally amazed. Then a voice said, 'Peter, go for it. It's a buffet.' I was like, 'No way, Boss. I've never eaten anything that wasn't 100% kosher.' But the voice came back, 'Look, if God says it's clean, it's clean.' This happened three times before the whole thing just zipped back up into the sky.

Right after that, three guys from Caesarea showed up looking for me. The Holy Spirit was like, 'Go with them, don't sweat the details.' So I took six of my boys and we went. The guy who sent for me told us this insane story about an angel just appearing in his house, telling him to send for me and that I'd have a message that would give him and his whole family a miraculous transformation. So I started talking, and I barely got a few words out before the Holy Spirit just showed up and hit them, just like it did for us at the beginning. It reminded me of what Jesus said: 'John just got you wet, but you're gonna be baptized by the Holy Spirit.' So, for real, if God is giving them the same exact gift he gave us when we started believing, who am I to get in God's way?"
§The Church in Antioch

When they heard that, everyone went quiet. It started to sink in, and then they started cheering for God. "Whoa, for real? God's even letting the outsiders in on this new life!" That's a total plot twist.

Meanwhile, all the people who got scattered when Stephen was taken out had traveled all over the place, as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. But they were still only talking to other Jews. Then, some of the guys from Cyprus and Cyrene who were in Antioch started talking to the Greeks, telling them all about Jesus. God was totally behind it, and a ton of Greeks believed and joined the team.

When the church in Jerusalem heard about this, they sent Barnabas to Antioch to see what was up. When he got there, he saw God's hand in all of it and was super stoked. He jumped right in, telling everyone to stick with God no matter what. Barnabas was a solid guy, full of the Holy Spirit and super enthusiastic. Because of him, the church got huge.

Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to find Saul. He found him and brought him back to Antioch. For a whole year, they hung out with the church, teaching tons of people. And it was in Antioch that the disciples first got the nickname "Christians."

Around that time, some prophets came to Antioch from Jerusalem. One of them, a guy named Agabus, stood up and, prompted by the Spirit, warned everyone that a massive famine was going to hit the whole country. (And it totally did, when Claudius was emperor). So the disciples decided to send a care package to the Christians in Judea. They each chipped in what they could and sent Barnabas and Saul to deliver it to the leaders in Jerusalem.

title: The Great Escape and a King's Epic Fail
paragraphs: §James Killed, Peter Arrested

So, this King Herod guy got it in his head to start messing with the church crew to score some popularity points. He went full-on villain and had James, John's brother, executed. When he saw that this made him look cool to some people, he decided to go after the main man, Peter. He had Peter arrested right in the middle of the Passover festival and thrown in a maximum-security prison. We're talking a whole squad of sixteen soldiers guarding him. Herod was planning a big public showdown after the festival.
§Peter's Miraculous Escape

But the whole time Peter was on lockdown, his friends in the church were praying like crazy for him. The night before Herod's big event, Peter was just chilling, fast asleep between two guards he was chained to. Suddenly, an angel appears and the whole cell gets a miraculous transformation. The angel nudges Peter awake and is like, "Hurry up!" and boom, the chains just fall off. The angel tells him, "Get dressed, put on your shoes, grab your coat, and let's bounce."

Peter followed, thinking he was having some kind of crazy dream. They walked right past the first and second guards, no problem. Then they get to the main iron gate of the city, and it just swings open for them automatically. They're out on the street, and then the angel just ghosts him. It's then that Peter realizes it's all real. He's like, "Whoa, God totally sent his angel to save me from Herod's evil plan!"
§Peter Knocks at Mary's Door

Still trying to process everything, Peter heads over to Mary's house, where a bunch of his friends were having a prayer meeting for him. He knocks on the door, and a girl named Rhoda comes to answer. She hears Peter's voice and gets so excited that she runs back to tell everyone without even opening the door, leaving Peter just standing there. The others are like, "Rhoda, you're tripping," but she keeps insisting. They're all arguing, saying, "It must be his ghost or something."

Meanwhile, Peter's still outside knocking. They finally open the door, see him, and everyone just loses it. Peter has to calm them down and explains how God broke him out of jail. He tells them to pass the message on to James (a different James) and the rest of the crew, and then he dips to another spot.

The next morning, the prison is in total chaos. "Where's Peter?!" Herod is furious when he finds out Peter is gone and, in a classic villain move, he orders all the guards who were on duty to be executed. After that, he peaces out of Judea and goes to chill in Caesarea for a bit.

Later, Herod is having a big public meeting with delegates from Tyre and Sidon, all dressed up in his royal robes, giving some big-shot speech. The crowd, trying to butter up to him, starts shouting, "It's the voice of a god, not a man!" Right then, because Herod was taking all the credit and not giving any props to God, an angel of the Lord strikes him down. He was eaten up by worms and died—rotten to the core. It was a total epic fail for him.

But even with all that drama, the message of God just kept spreading and getting more and more popular. Barnabas and Saul, after dropping off some help for the church in Jerusalem, headed back to Antioch, and this time they brought a guy named John Mark with them.

title: The Holy Spirit's Temple Guards
paragraphs: §Paul's First Mission Trip

So, the church in Antioch was stacked with some seriously gifted leaders. You had Barnabas, Simon (who they called Niger), Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen (who grew up with Herod, the governor!), and Saul. One day, while they were all worshiping and fasting, the Holy Spirit just drops in and says, "Hey, I need Barnabas and Saul for a special mission. Set them apart for the work I've got for them."
So, after more praying and fasting, the leaders laid their hands on them and sent them off. Talk about a power move!

Barnabas and Saul, now on a mission from God, headed down to Seleucia and hopped on a boat to Cyprus. First stop: Salamis. They immediately started preaching God's word in the Jewish synagogues, with John helping them out.
§Elymas the Sorcerer

They traveled across the whole island and ended up in Paphos. There, they ran into this suspicious guy named Bar-Jesus, a Jewish sorcerer who had somehow become buddies with the governor, Sergius Paulus. Now, the governor was a smart guy and wasn't easily fooled. He invited Barnabas and Saul to his place because he wanted to hear what they had to say about God.

But this sorcerer, this "Dr. Know-It-All," tried to shut them down. He was trying to keep the governor from believing. But Saul, who was also called Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit and just stared the guy down. "You're a total fraud!" he said. "You're a son of the devil, and you're always trying to twist God's truth. Well, guess what? You're done. You're going blind for a while." And just like that, the guy couldn't see a thing and was stumbling around, begging for someone to lead him by the hand.
When the governor saw this, he was blown away and became a believer. He was all in on what they were teaching about Jesus.
From there, Paul and his crew sailed to Perga. But that's where John bailed on them and went back to Jerusalem. The rest of them continued on to Antioch in Pisidia.
§Preaching in Antioch

On the Sabbath, they went to the synagogue and sat down. After the usual readings from the Law and the Prophets, the leader of the synagogue asked them, "Hey, you guys got anything to share? A word of encouragement, maybe?"

Paul stood up, took a deep breath, and went for it. "Alright, listen up, fellow Israelites and all you who fear God. Our God chose our ancestors and made them a great nation, even when they were slaves in Egypt. He flexed his power and led them out of there. He put up with them in the desert for forty years, and then he wiped out seven nations in Canaan to give them their own land. This all took about 450 years.

Then he gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet. But the people begged for a king, so God gave them Saul, who ruled for forty years. But Saul messed up, so God ghosted him and made David the new king. God said, 'I've found David, a man after my own heart. He'll do everything I want him to do.'

"And from David's family, God brought us the Savior, Jesus, just like he promised. But first, John the Baptist came and got everyone ready for him. John told people to turn their lives around. And as he was finishing his work, he said, 'I'm not the one you're waiting for. But he's coming soon, and I'm not even worthy to untie his sandals.'

"Brothers, this message of salvation is for you! The people in Jerusalem and their leaders didn't recognize Jesus. They condemned him to death, even though they couldn't find any reason to. They were just fulfilling what the prophets had written about him. After they killed him, they buried him. But God raised him from the dead! And he appeared to many people who had known him in Galilee, and they are his witnesses.

"We're here to tell you the good news. The promise God made to our ancestors has come true for us, their children. He raised Jesus from the dead, just like it says in the second Psalm: 'You are my Son; today I have become your Father.'

"God raised him from the dead, never to rot in a grave. This is what he meant when he said, 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.' And in another place it says, 'You will not let your Holy One see decay.'

"David died and was buried, but the one God raised from the dead never decayed. So, my friends, I want you to know that through Jesus, the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you. Through him, everyone who believes is set free from every sin, a freedom you could never get from the law of Moses.

"So watch out! Don't let what the prophets said happen to you: 'Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish, for I am going to do something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.'"

As Paul and Barnabas were leaving, the people invited them to come back next week and tell them more. After the service, many Jews and converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who urged them to continue in the grace of God.

The next Sabbath, almost the whole city came to hear the word of the Lord. But when some of the Jews saw the crowds, they got super jealous and started to argue with everything Paul was saying. They were being total haters.

But Paul and Barnabas weren't scared. They stood their ground and said, "We had to speak the word of God to you first. But since you've rejected it and don't consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we're moving on to the Gentiles. For this is what the Lord has commanded us: 'I have made you a light for the Gentiles, that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'"
When the Gentiles heard this, they were stoked. They praised the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life became believers. The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.

But some of the Jews stirred up trouble with the important women and the leading men of the city. They started a persecution against Paul and Barnabas and kicked them out of town. So Paul and Barnabas just shook the dust off their feet and went on to Iconium, filled with joy and the Holy Spirit. They were two happy disciples, ready for the next adventure.

title: Road Trip, Riots, and Getting Mistaken for Gods
paragraphs: §Iconium and Lystra

So Paul and Barnabas roll into Iconium and, like always, head straight to the Jewish meeting place to share their message. It was straight fire, and tons of people, both Jews and non-Jews, were convinced. But you know there are always haters. The Jews who weren't buying it started a vicious rumor campaign, trying to make everyone suspicious of Paul and Barnabas. But the two apostles didn't back down. They stayed for a long time, speaking freely and confidently about God's amazing grace, and God was flexing His power, backing them up with legit miracles and wonders.

Eventually, the town was split. Some people sided with the Jewish leaders, and others were with the apostles. One day, Paul and Barnabas heard that a mob of both Jews and non-Jews, stirred up by the leaders, was planning to rough them up. So they ghosted them and escaped to the nearby towns of Lystra and Derbe. But they didn't stop; they just started preaching the Message all over again there.

In Lystra, there was a guy who couldn't walk; he'd been crippled from birth. He was listening to Paul speak, and Paul looked him right in the eye and could just tell the guy was ready to believe—totally ripe for a God-sized transformation. So Paul yelled out, "Up on your feet!" The man was up in a flash, jumping and walking around like he'd been doing it his whole life.
§Mistaken for Gods

When the crowd saw this, they went absolutely wild. They started shouting in their local language, "The gods are here! They look like men!" They decided Barnabas was the big boss, Zeus, and since Paul did most of the talking, they called him Hermes, the messenger god. The priest from the local Zeus temple even organized a parade, bringing bulls and flowers to the city gates to throw a massive sacrifice for them.

When Paul and Barnabas finally figured out what was happening, they totally freaked out. They ran into the crowd, waving their arms and yelling, "Whoa, what are you guys doing?! We're not gods! We're just ordinary guys like you!" They were there to bring them the real story, to get them to ditch these fake god superstitions and turn to the one, true, living God who made everything—the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.

"For a long time," Paul explained, "God let all the nations do their own thing. But He never left you without clues. He sent rain, gave you good crops, filled your stomachs, and made you happy. That was all evidence of a good God looking out for you." Even with all that, they barely stopped the crowd from making a sacrifice to them.

Then, some of the haters from Antioch and Iconium showed up and totally flipped the script, turning the crowd against them. They stoned Paul, dragged him out of town, and left him for dead. But as his followers gathered around him, he got back up and went right back into town. The next day, he and Barnabas took off for Derbe.
§Back to Home Base

After sharing the Message in Derbe and getting a solid group of disciples going, they back-tracked to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch. They pumped up the new believers, telling them to stick with it and not give up, and made it super clear: signing up for God's kingdom means going through plenty of hard times.

Paul and Barnabas then handpicked leaders for each church. After some serious prayer and fasting, they put these new leaders in charge, trusting the Master with their lives. They traveled back through the regions of Pisidia and Pamphylia, preached in Perga, and finally made it to the port city of Attalia. From there, they sailed back to Antioch, right where their whole journey started, all by God's grace.

When they got back, they called a big church meeting and gave everyone the full report. They told them all the details of how God had used them to swing the door of faith wide open for people from all nations to come in. After that, they just chilled for a while, hanging out with the disciples.

title: The Ultimate Smackdown: Rules vs. Grace
paragraphs: §The Big Debate

So, not long after Paul and Barnabas got back, some guys from Judea showed up and started telling all the new non-Jewish believers that they had to get circumcised, like, for real. They were all like, "If you don't do this old-school ritual, you can't be saved." Total buzzkill.

Paul and Barnabas were not having it. They totally called them out, and things got heated. So, the church decided to send Paul, Barnabas, and a few other guys to Jerusalem to talk to the head honchos—the apostles and leaders—and get this whole thing sorted out. It was like a holy delegation on a mission for truth.

When they got to Jerusalem, the whole church, including the apostles and leaders, gave them a warm welcome. Paul and Barnabas told them all about their epic journey and how God was opening doors for people who weren't Jewish. But then, some of the believers who used to be Pharisees, the super-strict rule-followers, stood up and said, "Hold up! These new guys have to be circumcised and follow all of Moses' laws!" They were trying to put everyone in a spiritual straitjacket.
§The Decision

The apostles and leaders called a big meeting to figure this out. The debate went on forever, with everyone getting more and more worked up. Finally, Peter, the OG of the group, stood up and said, "Hey, listen up! You all know that way back, God chose me to be the one to bring the good news to the non-Jews. And God, who knows what's in everyone's hearts, gave them the Holy Spirit, just like he did for us. He didn't treat them any different. He cleaned up their lives from the inside out when they put their trust in him.

"So why are you trying to be more extra than God? Why are you trying to load up these new believers with a bunch of rules that even our own ancestors couldn't handle? We believe we're saved by the awesome generosity of Jesus, and so are they. So what's the big deal?"
Everyone went dead silent. You could hear a pin drop. Then, Barnabas and Paul shared all the insane miracles and wonders God had done through them among the non-Jews. The room got even quieter.

Then James, another one of the top leaders, spoke up. "Brothers, listen to me. Peter just told us how God made sure from the very beginning that the non-Jews were included. This lines up perfectly with what the old prophets said: 'After all this, I'll come back and rebuild everything that's been wrecked. I'll put it all back together, good as new. Then, anyone who's looking for God can find him, including all the people from every nation.' God knew this was the plan all along.

"So here's my call: we shouldn't make it super hard for the non-Jews who are turning to God. Let's just send them a letter and tell them to stay away from a few things: don't get mixed up in idol worship, keep it clean when it comes to sex and marriage, and don't eat food that would gross out our Jewish friends, like stuff with blood in it. This is just basic stuff that's been taught for ages."

Everyone agreed. They picked two solid guys, Judas (not the one who betrayed Jesus, a different one) and Silas, who were both big deals in the church, and sent them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They carried a letter that said:
"From your friends, the apostles and leaders, to all our friends in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: What's up!

We heard some guys from our group came and confused you with a bunch of stuff we didn't tell them to say. They were totally out of line. So, we all agreed to send some of our best guys to you, along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul, who have risked their lives for Jesus. We're sending Judas and Silas to tell you this in person.

It seemed like a good idea to the Holy Spirit and to us not to weigh you down with a bunch of rules. Just stick to the basics: stay away from idol stuff, don't eat bloody food, and keep your relationships pure. If you do that, you'll be golden. Peace out!"

So, the crew went to Antioch, gathered everyone together, and read the letter. The people were so relieved and happy. Judas and Silas, who were both awesome speakers, pumped everyone up with a ton of encouragement.
After a while, it was time for them to head home. They got a big, warm send-off from their new friends. But Paul and Barnabas decided to stick around in Antioch and keep teaching and preaching.

After a few days, Paul said to Barnabas, "Hey, let's go back and check on all our friends in the towns where we preached. Let's see how they're doing." Barnabas was down, and he wanted to bring his cousin, John Mark, along. But Paul was not having it. He was like, "No way! That guy ghosted us in the middle of our last trip when things got tough. He's a quitter."

Things got super tense, and they had a major blowout. They ended up splitting up. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus. Paul chose Silas, and after their friends prayed for them, they headed out to Syria and Cilicia to help the churches there get even stronger. It was a total bro-vorce, but God still used them both to do amazing things.

title: The Jailbreak Anthem
paragraphs: §Timothy Joins the Team

Paul rolled into the next town and met this kid, Timothy. Timothy’s mom was a believer, but his dad was a Greek, so the Jewish crew was a bit sus of him. Everyone said Timothy was a solid guy, so Paul was like, “You’re on my team now.” But first, to keep the peace, he had Timothy get circumcised so nobody could start any drama. After that, they bounced from town to town, sharing the new rules from the head honchos in Jerusalem. The local churches totally leveled up, getting bigger and stronger in their faith every day.

Paul and his crew tried to take their tour to Asia, but the Holy Spirit basically put up a big “ACCESS DENIED” sign. So they tried another route, but the Spirit of Jesus ghosted them again. They ended up at the coast, and that night, Paul had this wild dream where a guy from Macedonia was begging him, “Look, come over here and help us!” Paul woke up and knew it was a sign. It was like a divine GPS telling them, “Rerouting… to Europe.” They packed their bags immediately.

They sailed to Philippi, a major Roman city. On the Sabbath, they found a group of women praying by a river and joined them. One of them was Lydia, a total boss who sold expensive purple cloth. She was super into what Paul was saying, and God opened her heart. She and her entire household got baptized right away. Then she insisted they stay at her house, giving them the full special treatment. She wouldn’t take no for an answer.
§The Slave Girl

One day, this slave girl who could supposedly tell the future started following them around, yelling, “These guys work for the Most High God! They’re showing you the way to be saved!” She was making her owners a ton of money with her psychic act. After a few days of this, Paul got fed up. He turned around and said to the spirit inside her, “In the name of Jesus Christ, get out!” And just like that, it was gone.

Well, her owners were furious. Their cash cow was gone. They grabbed Paul and Silas, roughed them up, and dragged them to the town square, accusing them of being troublemakers. The crowd turned into a mob, and the judges, caving to the pressure, had Paul and Silas stripped, beaten black-and-blue, and thrown into the maximum-security part of the jail. The jailer even clamped their feet in stocks.
§The Philippian Jailer

Around midnight, Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns so loud the other prisoners were probably thinking they were crazy. Suddenly, a massive earthquake stunned the whole prison. The doors flew open, and everyone’s chains fell off! The jailer woke up, saw the open doors, and freaked out, thinking everyone had escaped. He was about to kill himself when Paul yelled, “Chill! We’re all still here!”

The terrified jailer ran in, fell at their feet, and asked, “Sirs, what do I have to do to be saved?” They told him, “Put your trust in the Master Jesus, and you and your whole family will be saved.” They explained the whole story of Jesus to him and his family. The jailer cleaned their wounds, and then he and his entire family were baptized that very night. He threw a huge party for them; it was an all-night celebration because they had all put their trust in God.

The next morning, the city officials sent a message: “Let those guys go.” But Paul wasn’t having it. He told the officers, “They beat us in public without a trial and threw us in jail, even though we’re Roman citizens! And now they want to sneak us out? No way. Let them come and escort us out themselves.” When the officials heard they were Roman citizens, they panicked. They rushed over, apologized like crazy, and personally walked them out of the jail, begging them to leave the city. Paul and Silas went to Lydia’s house, encouraged their friends, and then finally hit the road.

title: Paul Starts a Riot (Whoops!)
paragraphs: §Thessalonica and Berea

Paul and his crew rolled into Thessalonica and, like always, Paul headed straight for the synagogue. For three weeks straight, he basically held a masterclass, breaking down the scriptures. He was like, "Listen up! The Messiah *had* to die and have a miraculous transformation by coming back to life. No other way. And guess what? This Jesus I've been telling you about? He's the guy."

Some people were totally convinced and joined Paul and Silas's squad, including a bunch of Greeks who were into God and even some prominent women. But the old-school religious leaders were seriously salty about all the new followers. They got super jealous, hired a mob of random thugs, and started a riot, trying to hunt down Paul and Silas.

They busted into this guy Jason's house, thinking Paul and Silas were hiding out there. When they couldn't find them, they grabbed Jason and his friends and dragged them in front of the city officials, screaming, "These guys are trying to flip the world upside down, and now they're here! Jason's even helping them! They're saying some guy named Jesus is the real king, not Caesar!"
§Trouble in Berea
The whole city was in an uproar. The officials made Jason and his buddies pay a ton of money as a security deposit and told them to chill while they figured things out.

That night, Paul and Silas's friends snuck them out of town and sent them to Berea. The people there were way cooler. They were super into Paul's message and actually checked the scriptures every day to see if he was legit. A lot of them started believing, including some really important Greek men and women.

But, of course, the drama followed them. The haters from Thessalonica heard Paul was preaching in Berea and came over to start another mob. So Paul's friends helped him dip out, and he hopped on a boat. Silas and Timothy stayed behind. The guys who helped Paul escape took him all the way to Athens and then bounced, but not before Paul told them to tell Silas and Timothy to hurry up and meet him.
§Paul in Athens

While Paul was waiting in Athens, he got more and more furious. The whole city was like a museum of fake gods. He argued with the religious people at the synagogue and then went out and debated anyone he could find on the street. He even got into it with some brainy philosophers. Some of them said, "This guy is a total moron," but others who heard him talking about Jesus and the resurrection said, "Whoa, that's a new take. Tell us more."

They took him to a big open meeting place called the Areopagus to give a formal presentation. "This is some wild new teaching," they said. "We've never heard this before. Spill the tea." See, everyone in Athens, locals and tourists, just loved to gossip and hear the latest hot take.

So Paul stood up and went for it. "Okay, people of Athens, I can see you're all super religious. I was walking around and saw all your shrines, and I even found one that said, 'To the Unknown God.' Well, I'm here to introduce you to him, so you can stop guessing and know who you're actually dealing with.

"The God who made the entire universe doesn't live in some little temple you built. He doesn't need us to do stuff for him, like he's helpless. He made us; we didn't make him. He created all of humanity from one person and gave us the whole world to live in so we could search for him and find him. And he's not playing hide-and-seek; he's right here. We live and move and exist in him. One of your own poets even said, 'We are his offspring.' So if we're God's kids, does it really make sense to think we can just carve a god out of gold or stone?

"God let it slide when you didn't know any better, but that time's over. Now that you know the truth, he's calling everyone to make a major life change. He's set a day to judge the whole world and make everything right. And he's already picked the judge and proved it to everyone by raising him from the dead."

When he said "raising him from the dead," the crowd was split. Some of them just laughed and walked away, making jokes. Others said, "We want to hear more about this later." So Paul left. But a few people were convinced right then and there and stuck with Paul, including a guy named Dionysius, who was a member of the Areopagus, and a woman named Damaris.

title: Paul’s New Crew and a Surprise Pep Talk
paragraphs: §Paul in Corinth

So after his trip to Athens, Paul bounced over to Corinth. There, he met this awesome couple, Aquila and Priscilla. They’d just been kicked out of Italy because the emperor, Claudius, was being a total hater to all the Jews in Rome. Paul crashed with them, and since they were all tentmakers, they started a little business together. Every weekend, Paul would hit up the local synagogue and try to get everyone, Jews and Greeks, hyped about Jesus.

When his buddies Silas and Timothy showed up from Macedonia, Paul went full-time into preaching mode. He was all in, trying to show the Jews that Jesus was the real deal, the Messiah they'd been waiting for. But they were not having it. They just argued and dissed everything he said. Paul got so fed up he was like, “Alright, I’m out. You guys do you. I’m gonna go talk to people who actually want to listen.”

He bounced and went to hang out at the house of Titius Justus, a man who was super into God and lived right next door to the synagogue. But it wasn’t a total wash with the Jews, ‘cause the head of the synagogue, Crispus, and his whole family started believing in Jesus. And a ton of other people in Corinth who heard Paul’s message believed and got baptized. One night, Jesus came to Paul in a dream and was like, “Don’t stop. Don’t let anyone shut you up. I’ve got your back, and no one’s gonna mess with you. I’ve got a huge squad in this city.” That was all Paul needed to hear. He stuck around for another year and a half, teaching everyone about God.
§Paul Before Gallio

But then, when a new governor named Gallio was in charge, some of the Jews ganged up on Paul and dragged him to court. They were like, “This guy is trying to get people to worship God in a way that’s against the rules!”

Just as Paul was about to say something, Gallio cut in and told the Jews, “Look, if he’d committed a crime, I’d listen. But this is just you guys arguing about your religion. Deal with it yourselves. I’m not wasting my time with this.” And he kicked them out of the courtroom. Then, the crowd grabbed the new synagogue leader, Sosthenes, and beat him up right there in front of everyone. Gallio just shrugged, like he couldn’t care less.

Paul hung out in Corinth for a while longer, then it was time to go. He said bye to his friends and sailed to Syria with Priscilla and Aquila. Before they left, he shaved his head to show he was keeping a promise he’d made to God.

They landed in Ephesus, and Priscilla and Aquila stayed there. Paul popped into the synagogue to talk to the Jews for a bit. They wanted him to stay longer, but he was like, “Nah, I gotta go. But I’ll come back if God’s cool with it.”
§Back to Antioch

From there, he sailed to Caesarea, said hi to the church, and then went on to Antioch. After chilling with the Christians in Antioch for a while, Paul hit the road again, visiting all the towns in Galatia and Phrygia and getting all the believers fired up.

Meanwhile, this guy named Apollos showed up in Ephesus. He was from Alexandria in Egypt and was a super-talented speaker who knew the Scriptures inside and out. He was all about Jesus and taught everything he knew, but he only knew up to what John the Baptist had taught. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they pulled him aside and gave him the full scoop. When Apollos decided to go to Achaia, his new friends in Ephesus wrote him a letter of recommendation, telling the believers there to welcome him. And it was a good thing they did, because he was a huge help to them. He would publicly refute his opponents, using the Scriptures to prove that Jesus was the Messiah.

title: God's Power Flex & A Massive Riot
paragraphs: §Paul in Ephesus

So, while this guy Apollos was in Corinth, Paul was trekking through the mountains and ended up in Ephesus. He found some believers there and right away asked them, "Hey, did you get the Holy Spirit when you started believing? Like, is God really with you, or just an idea in your head?"
They said, "Look, we've never even heard of a 'Holy Spirit.' God *in* us? What's that?"
Paul was like, "Huh? Then what kind of baptism did you have?"
§Baptized in Jesus' Name
"John's baptism," they said.

"Okay, that makes sense," Paul explained. "John's baptism was all about a major life-change to get everyone hyped for the guy coming after him, who turned out to be Jesus. If you got John's baptism, you're totally ready for the real deal, for Jesus."

And they were! The moment they heard this, they got baptized in the name of Jesus. Then Paul put his hands on them, and BAM! The Holy Spirit came on them. They started speaking in different languages and talking about all the awesome stuff God was doing. There were about twelve of them there.

Paul then rolled into the local synagogue and for three months, he was basically the main event. He was trying his best to show them that God's kingdom was for real. But some people started getting salty and spreading vicious rumors about this new "Way" of life. So, Paul bounced, took his crew with him, and started holding daily classes at a school owned by some guy named Tyrannus. He did this for two whole years, so pretty much everyone in that part of Asia, whether they were Jewish or Greek, got to hear about Jesus.

God was doing some seriously next-level stuff through Paul. It got so crazy that people would take handkerchiefs and aprons that Paul had touched and use them on sick people. And it worked! They were instantly healed.

Then, some wannabe Jewish exorcists who were just passing through town tried to get in on the action. They started using Jesus' name to cast out evil spirits, saying stuff like, "I command you by the Jesus that Paul preaches about!" Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva tried this on a guy, but the evil spirit clapped back, "I know Jesus, and I've heard of Paul, but who the heck are you guys?" Then the man with the evil spirit went totally nuts, jumped on all seven of them, and beat them so bad they ran out of the house naked and bleeding. It was a total beatdown.

Word about this got out all over Ephesus, and everyone, Jews and Greeks, were stunned. They realized God's power was the real deal, and they started showing major respect for Jesus. A bunch of people who had been into black magic and sorcery came forward and confessed everything. They brought all their spell books and had a massive bonfire. Someone did the math, and all those books were worth a fortune—like fifty thousand silver coins! This just showed that Jesus' message was taking over and winning big time in Ephesus.

After all this craziness, Paul decided it was time to head to Macedonia and Achaia, and then to Jerusalem. "And after that," he said, "I've gotta see Rome!" He sent two of his buddies, Timothy and Erastus, ahead to Macedonia while he wrapped things up in Asia.
§The Riot

But before he could leave, a massive riot broke out because of "the Way." A silversmith named Demetrius, who made a ton of money selling little silver shrines of the goddess Artemis, got all his workers and other craftsmen together. He said, "Guys, you know we make a killing from this business. But this Paul guy has come in and is totally dissing our work, telling people that gods made by humans are fake. And tons of people are believing him, not just here but all over the province!
