"This is bad for business, and even worse, the temple of our awesome goddess Artemis is going to become worthless! Her rep is going to be toast, and she's worshipped by the whole world!"

That was it. The crowd went wild. They started screaming, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" They caused a huge uproar, dragged two of Paul's friends, Gaius and Aristarchus, into the city's stadium. Paul wanted to go in and face the mob, but his friends and even some of the city officials who liked him begged him not to.

The whole stadium was a chaotic mess. Most people didn't even know why they were there. Some people pushed a guy named Alexander to the front to try and calm everyone down, but as soon as he opened his mouth and they realized he was a Jew, they just shouted him down, yelling "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" for two straight hours.

Finally, the city clerk managed to quiet the crowd. "People of Ephesus!" he shouted. "Who doesn't know that our city is the protector of the great goddess Artemis and her sacred stone that fell from heaven? This is a fact, so you all need to chill out. You're acting a fool. These guys you dragged in here haven't robbed our temple or said anything bad about our goddess.

"If Demetrius and his crew have a problem, they can take it to court. If you have other issues, bring them up at the next official city meeting. What you did today was not cool. We're in big trouble with Rome because of this riot." And with that, he told everyone to go home.

title: Paul's Epic Farewell Tour
paragraphs: §Traveling Through Greece

After things chilled out in Ephesus, Paul gathered his crew and was like, "Keep crushing it, guys!" Then he bounced to Macedonia, going all over the place and hyping everyone up. He was like a walking pep rally.

He hung out in Greece for three months, but just when he was about to sail to Syria, some haters tried to pull a fast one. So Paul was like, "Nah," and dipped out, taking the scenic route through Macedonia to dodge them. He rolled with his squad: Sopater, Aristarchus, Secundus, Gaius, Timothy, and his boys from Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
His crew went ahead to Troas to wait for him. Paul and his group stayed in Philippi for Passover and then set sail. Five days later, they were all reunited in Troas, where they hung out for a week.

On Sunday, they all got together to worship and have a meal to remember Jesus. Paul was giving a talk, and he just kept going... and going... way past midnight. They were in this lit-up room on the third floor. This one kid, Eutychus, was sitting in the window, and he totally conked out. He fell right out of the window, three stories down. When they got to him, he was gone. Total tragedy.
§The Kid Who Fell Out the Window

But then Paul went down, hugged the kid, and was like, "Don't trip, he's still breathing." Then he went back upstairs, served communion, and kept telling stories until the sun came up! They all left, with the kid totally fine, and everyone was buzzing. What a transformation for Eutychus!

Paul's crew sailed on to Assos, but Paul decided to walk. He met up with them there, and they sailed to Mitylene, then Chios, then Samos, and finally Miletus. Paul was in a hurry to get to Jerusalem for Pentecost, so he skipped Ephesus to avoid getting held up.
§Paul's Farewell Speech

From Miletus, he sent a message to the church leaders in Ephesus to come meet him. When they showed up, he gave them the real talk: "You guys know I've been 100% with you from day one, serving God no matter what, even when people were plotting against me. I never held back. I told you everything you needed to know, in public and in your homes, telling everyone to turn to God and trust in Jesus.

"And now, I've got to go to Jerusalem. I have no idea what's going to happen to me there, but the Holy Spirit has been warning me that I'm in for some hard times and even jail. But honestly, I don't even care. All that matters is that I finish the job Jesus gave me: telling everyone about God's insane generosity.

"So, this is it. We're not going to see each other again. I've done my best to tell you everything about God's kingdom. Now it's on you. You've got to watch out for yourselves and for the church. The Holy Spirit put you in charge, so you have to protect God's people. He thought they were worth dying for.

"I know that as soon as I'm gone, some serious phonies are going to show up and try to mess things up. They'll even come from your own group, twisting the truth to get people to follow them instead of Jesus. So stay woke! Remember how I poured my heart out to you guys for three years straight?

"I'm leaving you in God's hands. His awesome word can build you up and give you everything you need. I've never been about money or fancy stuff. I worked with my own hands to support myself and my crew. I've shown you that you've got to help people who are struggling, not take advantage of them. Like Jesus said, 'It's way better to give than to get.'"

Then they all knelt and prayed together. There were a lot of tears. Everyone was hugging Paul, not wanting to let him go. They were totally gutted because he told them they'd never see him again. It was a super emotional goodbye as they walked him to the ship.

title: Paul vs. The World
paragraphs: §Heading to Jerusalem

So after a super emotional goodbye where everyone was bawling their eyes out, we bounced. We made a beeline for Cos, then hit up Rhodes the next day, and then Patara. We found a ship heading straight to Phoenicia, so we hopped on. We saw Cyprus for a hot second, but then it was out of sight as we kept cruising to Syria. We finally docked in Tyre. While they were unloading the cargo, we found some local believers and crashed with them for a week. They got a message from the Holy Spirit and were like, “Look, for real, don’t go to Jerusalem. It’s a trap!”

When our week was up, the whole crew—guys, ladies, and kids—walked us to the docks. It was a total farewell party! We all knelt on the beach and prayed. After another round of goodbyes, we got on the ship, and they all went home.

It was a quick trip from Tyre to Ptolemais. We said what’s up to our Christian friends there and stayed for a day. The next morning, we were off to Caesarea and stayed with Philip the Evangelist, one of the original seven deacons. Fun fact: Philip had four daughters who were all prophets.
§Agabus's Warning

After a few days of chilling, a prophet named Agabus from Judea came to see us. He walked right up to Paul, snatched his belt, and in a dramatic prophetic gesture, tied his own hands and feet with it. Then he goes, “The Holy Spirit says this: The man who owns this belt is gonna get tied up just like this by the Jews in Jerusalem and handed over to the Gentiles.”

When we heard that, we and everyone else there begged Paul not to be so stubborn and just ghost Jerusalem. But Paul was like, “Hey, why are you all panicking? You’re making this way harder for me. You’re looking at it all wrong. It’s not about what they do to me in Jerusalem, whether they arrest me or kill me. It’s about what the Master Jesus does through me when I obey. Don’t you get it?”
We realized we couldn’t change his mind, so we just gave up. “It’s in God’s hands now,” we said. “You do you, Master.”

Soon after, we packed our bags and headed to Jerusalem. Some of the believers from Caesarea came with us and took us to Mnason’s house. He was super welcoming. He was from Cyprus and was one of the OG disciples.

In Jerusalem, our friends were stoked to see us and gave us a huge welcome. The next morning, we took Paul to see James, the head honcho of the Jerusalem church. All the church leaders were there too. After catching up, Paul told them everything, play-by-play, about how God had been working among the non-Jews through his ministry. They were totally blown away and gave God a massive shout-out.

Then they were like, “Look, you won’t believe what’s been happening here. Thousands of Jews who are all about God have become believers in Jesus! But here’s the tea: they’re also super intense about following the laws of Moses. And they’ve heard some rumors that you’re telling Jews who live around non-Jews to chill out on the old rules, like not circumcising their kids or keeping up the traditions. They are not happy about it.”

“We’re kinda worried about what’s gonna happen when they find out you’re in town. It’s gonna be a whole thing. So here’s the plan: we’ve got four guys here who made a vow to do a purification ritual, but they’re broke. You should join them and pay for their expenses. That way, everyone will see that the rumors are fake news and that you’re actually all about respecting the laws of Moses.”

“And don’t worry, we’re not changing our minds about the non-Jews who are believers. We still stand by what we wrote in that letter: they just need to stay away from anything to do with idols, not eat food that would gross out Jewish Christians, and keep it clean when it comes to sex and marriage.”

So Paul did it. He took the four guys, joined their vow, and paid for everything. The next day, he went to the Temple to make it official and stayed there until all the sacrifices were done for each of them.
§Paul Arrested

When the seven days of the purification were almost over, some Jews from around Ephesus saw him in the Temple. They immediately started a riot. They grabbed Paul and started screaming, “Help! Israelites, help! This is the guy who’s going all over the world, roasting our religion and this holy place. He even brought Greeks in here and contaminated it!” (What really happened was they saw Paul walking in the city with Trophimus, who was a Greek from Ephesus, and just assumed he brought him into the Temple.)

Soon the whole city was in an uproar. People were running from everywhere to the Temple to see what was going on. They grabbed Paul, dragged him outside, and locked the Temple gates so he couldn’t get back in and claim sanctuary.

While they were trying to kill him, someone told the captain of the guard, “There’s a massive riot! The whole city is going crazy!” He acted fast. He and his soldiers ran to the scene. As soon as the mob saw the captain and his soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

The captain arrested Paul and had him handcuffed. Then he asked who he was and what he had done. But all he got was a bunch of shouting from the crowd. It was impossible to understand anything in the chaos, so the captain ordered Paul to be taken to the military barracks. But when they got to the Temple steps, the mob got so violent that the soldiers had to carry Paul. As they carried him away, the crowd followed, screaming, “Kill him! Kill him!”
When they were about to go into the barracks, Paul said to the captain, “Can I say something to you?”
The captain was surprised. “Oh, you speak Greek? I thought you were that Egyptian guy who started a riot a while back and then hid in the desert with his four thousand troublemakers.”
Paul was like, “Nah, I’m a Jew, born in Tarsus, a pretty important city. I just have one request: let me talk to the crowd.”
Standing on the barracks steps, Paul raised his arms. The crowd went silent. Then Paul started to speak. He spoke in Hebrew.

title: Paul's Epic Monologue
paragraphs: §Paul's Defense Speech
"Hey, listen up, my guys and dads! Before you totally cancel me, just hear me out." When the crowd heard him speaking their language, they went dead silent. This was gonna be good.

Paul went on, "I'm a legit Jew, born in Tarsus, but I grew up right here in Jerusalem. I was top of my class, studied under the famous Gamaliel, and knew our traditions inside and out. I was super passionate about God, just like you guys are right now.

"I was so hardcore, I went after anyone who followed 'The Way.' I was ready to take them down for God. I had guys and girls arrested and thrown in jail. The head priest and the whole council can back me up on this; they knew what I was about. I even got official papers to go to Damascus and hunt down more of Jesus' followers to bring them back for punishment.
§Blinded by the Light

"But then, as I was getting close to Damascus around noon, this insane light from the sky just blasted me. I hit the ground, totally stunned. Then I heard a voice, 'Saul, Saul, why are you trying to cancel me?'
"I was like, 'Who are you, sir?'
"And the voice said, 'I'm Jesus of Nazareth, the one you're hunting.' My crew saw the light, but they didn't hear the voice.
"So I asked, 'What's the plan, sir?'

"He told me, 'Get up and go into Damascus. You'll get the full download there.' So we went into the city, but I was completely blind. My friends had to lead me by the hand. It was not the grand entrance I had in mind.

"That's when I met this guy Ananias. He was a super respected guy who followed all our laws—everyone in the Jewish community in Damascus vouched for him. He came over, put his hand on my shoulder, and said, 'Look up.' And just like that, I could see again! I was looking right at him.

"Then he told me, 'The God of our ancestors chose you to know his game plan. You've actually seen the real deal, the Righteous One, and heard him speak. You're going to be his witness and tell everyone what you've seen and heard. So what are you waiting for? Get up, get baptized, and wash away your sins. It's time to get to know God for real.'

"And it all went down just like Ananias said. Later, I was back in Jerusalem, praying in the Temple, totally in the zone, when I saw him—the Righteous One. He told me, 'Hurry! Get out of Jerusalem now. Nobody here is going to believe what you say about me.'

"I tried to argue, like, 'But I'm the perfect guy for the job! They all know how I used to hunt down your followers, beat them up, and throw them in jail. I was even there when your boy Stephen was killed, holding the coats for the guys who did it and cheering them on. Now they see me completely flipped. Wouldn't that make them listen?'
"But he was like, 'Don't argue. Just go. I'm sending you on a mission to the outsiders, the non-Jews.'"

The crowd was actually listening until he said that. Then they totally lost it. They started screaming, "Get rid of him! He doesn't deserve to live!" They were shaking their fists and cursing like crazy. The captain had to step in and ordered his soldiers to take Paul into the barracks. He was so done with the drama and decided to torture Paul to get the truth out of him and find out why everyone was so triggered.
As they were tying Paul up to whip him, he casually said to the centurion standing there, "Is it even legal to torture a Roman citizen who hasn't had a fair trial?"
When the centurion heard that, he ran to the captain. "Uh, you might want to rethink this. This guy is a Roman citizen!"
The captain rushed back and was like, "For real? You're a Roman citizen?"
Paul was like, "Yup. Sure am."
The captain was stunned. "I had to pay a ton of money for my citizenship. How much did you pay?"
"Nothing," Paul said. "I was born with it."
That shut down the whole interrogation. The captain was terrified. He had just chained up a Roman citizen and almost had him tortured. Big yikes.

The next day, the captain was still trying to figure out what the deal was with the Jews' accusations. So he let Paul go and called a meeting with the high priests and the council to sort things out. Paul was brought in and stood before them, ready for round two.

title: The Ultimate Informer and a Prison Break
paragraphs: §Before the Council

Paul stared down the whole council and was like, "For real, I've lived my whole life with a clean slate before God, seriously." That totally set off the head priest, Ananias. He ordered his guards to strike Paul right in the mouth. Paul shot back instantly, "God's gonna strike you right back, you phony! You sit there acting like you're all about the rules, but then you break them by ordering me to get hit? What a fake."

The guys standing by were shocked. "You can't just roast God's high priest like that!" Paul, playing it cool, was like, "Seriously? I had no idea he was the head priest. He sure doesn't act like one. You're right, the scripture says you shouldn't bad-mouth a leader. My bad."

Then Paul, knowing the council was split between two rival crews—the Sadducees and the Pharisees—who totally hated each other, decided to stir the pot. He yelled, "Bros, I'm a Pharisee, through and through! The only reason I'm on trial here is because I believe in the ultimate transformation after you die—the resurrection!"

The second he said that, the whole room exploded. The Pharisees and Sadducees started going at it. See, the Sadducees don't believe in resurrection, angels, or any of that spiritual stuff. If they can't see it, it's not real to them. But the Pharisees believe all of it. A massive fight broke out, and some of the Pharisee teachers started shouting, "We don't see anything wrong with this guy! What if a spirit or an angel actually talked to him? Are we trying to pick a fight with God himself?"

That just added fuel to the fire. The argument got so heated that the Roman commander was afraid they were literally going to tear Paul to pieces. He had to order his soldiers to charge in, grab Paul, and get him back to the safety of the army barracks.
That night, Jesus showed up to Paul and said, "Don't sweat it. It's all good. You've been an awesome witness for me here in Jerusalem. Now, you're gonna do the same thing in Rome!"
§Plot to Kill Paul

But the next day, a bunch of Paul's haters cooked up a crazy plot. More than forty of them made a super-serious oath not to eat or drink anything until they killed Paul. This group of men went to the priests and leaders and said, "We've sworn to ghost Paul for good. We need you to do us a solid. Get the council to ask the commander to bring Paul back tomorrow, pretending you need to ask him more questions. We'll be waiting to ambush him. He'll be gone before he even gets to you."

But Paul's nephew, his sister's son, overheard the whole plan. He ran to the barracks and told Paul everything. Paul called over a centurion and said, "Take this kid to the commander. He's got some major tea to spill."

The centurion took the nephew to the commander and said, "The prisoner, Paul, asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something important to tell you." The commander took the kid aside privately and asked, "What's up? What's the secret?"

Paul's nephew laid it all out: "The Jews have a hit out on Paul. They're going to ask you to bring him to their council tomorrow, but it's a trap to murder him. There are over forty guys in an ambush, and they've all sworn not to eat or drink until he's dead. They're all set and just waiting for you to give the green light."
The commander sent the nephew away with a warning: "Don't tell a soul you told me."

Then the commander called two of his centurions. "Get a squad ready. I need 200 soldiers, 70 on horseback, and 200 spearmen ready to roll out for Caesarea by 9 PM tonight. Get a couple of mules for Paul and his stuff, too. We're delivering this man to Governor Felix, safe and sound."
He also wrote a letter to the governor:
*From: Claudius Lysias
§The Commander's Letter
Greetings!

I had to rescue this man from a local mob that was about to kill him when I found out he was a Roman citizen. I brought him before their council to figure out what he did wrong, and it turns out it was just some internal drama about their religion, nothing criminal.

Then, I got intel that there was a murder plot against him. I decided it was best to get him out of here ASAP for his own safety. So, I'm sending him to you. I've told his accusers they'll have to make their case in your court.*

The soldiers followed their orders, taking Paul that night as far as Antipatris. The next morning, the foot soldiers headed back to Jerusalem, and the cavalry took Paul the rest of the way to Caesarea. They arrived, handed the governor the letter, and turned Paul over.

After reading the letter, the governor asked Paul where he was from. "Cilicia," Paul answered. The governor said, "Alright, I'll hear your case once your accusers get here." In the meantime, he had Paul locked up under guard in King Herod's swanky headquarters.

title: Paul vs. The Haters in Court
paragraphs: §Trial Before Felix
Five days later, the head priest, Ananias, showed up with his crew and a slick lawyer named Tertullus. They went straight to Governor Felix to start throwing shade at Paul.

When it was his turn, Tertullus started by totally buttering up Felix, saying, “Hey, Governor Felix, you’re the GOAT. Thanks to you, everything is chill and our lives are way better. For real. I’m not gonna waste your time, so I’ll keep it short.”

Then he pointed at Paul. “This guy is a major problem. He’s been going all over the world stirring up trouble with the Jews. He’s the ringleader of this suspicious group called the Nazarenes. Total bad news. We caught him trying to mess up our holy Temple, so we arrested him. You can grill him yourself and see that we’re telling the truth.”
"But then Commander Lysias showed up, grabbed Paul out of our hands, and ordered us to bring our charges to you. Question Paul yourself and you'll see that everything we're accusing him of is true."
The other Jews with him were all like, “Yeah, he’s right! That’s what happened!”

Then the governor gave Paul the nod to speak. Paul was like, “I’m actually stoked to be here, Governor, because I know you’re a fair guy. You can check the facts: I’ve only been in town for twelve days. I came to worship, not to start drama. Nobody saw me arguing in the Temple or starting riots in the streets. They have zero proof for any of their accusations. Seriously.

“But I’ll admit this: I follow ‘the Way,’ which they call a cult. But I’m worshipping the same God our ancestors did, and I believe everything written in the Scriptures. And I’m holding out for the ultimate transformation when God brings everyone back from the dead, good and bad. If that’s a crime, then my accusers are just as guilty.

“Look, I just try to keep a clear conscience with God and people. I was out of the country for a few years, and I came back to bring some money for the poor and make offerings at the Temple. That’s where they found me, just quietly doing my thing. No crowd, no noise. It was some guys from Ephesus who started all this, but they’re not even here to face me. They totally ghosted.

“So ask these guys what they actually saw me do. The only thing they can pin on me is when I shouted in their council, ‘I’m on trial today because I believe in the resurrection!’ Is that really a crime?”

Felix, who actually knew a lot about the Way, didn’t want to make a decision. He was playing politics. So he stalled and said, “I’ll figure this out when Captain Lysias gets here.” He told the guard to keep Paul in custody but give him some freedom and let his friends bring him stuff.

A few days later, Felix and his wife Drusilla (who was Jewish) sent for Paul to hear him talk about believing in Jesus. But when Paul started going on about living right, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix got super uncomfortable. He was like, “Okay, that’s enough for today. I’ll call you later.” He was also secretly hoping Paul would offer him a bribe to get out of jail. They had a bunch more of these chats.
Two years went by, and then Porcius Festus took over as governor. Felix, still trying to be popular with the Jews, just left Paul sitting in prison. What a snake.

title: Paul Pulls the Ultimate Power Move
paragraphs: §Paul Appeals to Caesar

So, this new governor, Festus, barely had time to unpack his bags in Caesarea before he shot up to Jerusalem. Three days in, and the top priests and Jewish leaders were already in his ear, trying to get him to do their dirty work. They were still super salty about Paul and wanted him gone. They said, "Hey Festus, my guy, could you do us a solid and bring Paul to Jerusalem for his trial?" But it was a total scam. They were planning to have a group of assassins ambush Paul on the way and take him out for good.

But Festus wasn't a total noob. He was like, "Nah, I'm not doing that. Paul's staying in Caesarea. I'm heading back in a few days, so if you've got beef with him, you can come with me and say it to his face." He wasn't about to let them play him.

A week or so later, Festus is back in Caesarea and drags Paul into the courtroom. The second Paul walks in, the guys from Jerusalem start throwing all sorts of wild accusations at him, but they had zero proof to back it up. Paul just stands there, cool as a cucumber, and says, "I haven't done anything wrong. Not against our religion, not against the Temple, and definitely not against Caesar. Period."

Festus, trying to be a people-pleaser, turns to Paul and says, "So, how about we just take this whole show on the road to Jerusalem?" But Paul wasn't having it. He knew what was up. He looked Festus dead in the eye and said, "I'm a Roman citizen, and I'm standing in Caesar's court. I've done nothing wrong, and you know it. If I've actually committed a crime worthy of death, then fine, let's do it. But if these guys are just making stuff up, you can't just hand me over to them. I've had enough of this nonsense. I'm taking this to the top. I appeal to Caesar!"
Festus was stunned. He had a quick huddle with his advisors and then came back and said, "You appealed to Caesar? Fine. To Caesar you will go!"

A few days later, King Agrippa and his wife, Bernice, roll into town to say hi to the new governor. After a few days of chilling, Festus brings up Paul's case. "So, I've got this prisoner, Paul, that the last governor, Felix, left behind. When I was in Jerusalem, the Jewish leaders were all over me, wanting me to sentence him to death. I told them that's not how we Romans roll. We don't just ghost someone because of accusations. The guy gets to face his accusers and defend himself.

"So, I brought him to trial, and you won't believe what their beef was about. It was all about their religion and some dead guy named Jesus, who Paul claims is alive. I'm new here and this is all way above my pay grade, so I asked Paul if he wanted to go to Jerusalem to be tried. He said no way and demanded a trial with the big boss, Caesar. So, I've got him on lockdown until I can ship him off to Rome."
Agrippa was intrigued. "I'd actually like to hear this guy's story for myself," he said. "Sweet," said Festus. "First thing tomorrow, you'll get your wish."

The next day, it was a full-on media circus. All the important people in Caesarea, including the top military brass, packed into the Great Hall. Agrippa and Bernice made a grand entrance, and then Festus had Paul brought in. Festus stood up and said, "King Agrippa, and all you distinguished guests, check out this guy. The Jews have been constantly demanding, wanting me to execute him. But after looking into it, I can't find anything he's done wrong. He's the one who asked to see Caesar, so I'm sending him to Rome. But here's the thing: I have no idea what to write in my report to Caesar. The Jews' accusations were all bogus, and I've got nothing else. That's why I've brought him before you all, and especially you, King Agrippa. I'm hoping you can help me come up with some actual charges that will stick. It's pretty lame to send a prisoner all that way without even being able to say what he did wrong."

title: Paul's Epic Monologue
paragraphs: §Paul Before King Agrippa
Agrippa, the big shot, gives Paul the floor. "Alright, Paul, spill the tea. Tell us your story."

Paul, not missing a beat, steps up and starts his epic monologue. "King Agrippa, my guy, I'm actually stoked to be telling you my side of the story. You're, like, the expert on all things Jewish, so you'll get it.

"Basically, my whole life, everyone in Jerusalem knew me. I was a super-strict Pharisee, the most hardcore of the hardcore. And if they weren't haters, they'd tell you themselves. The only reason I'm in trouble is because I actually believe God keeps his promises. The same promises our ancestors have been waiting for forever. And for some reason, the Jews are salty about it. Like, why is it a crime to believe God can bring people back from the dead? Make it make sense.

"I'll admit, I wasn't always on Team Jesus. For a while, I was a one-man army against him. I had the high priests' permission to throw believers in jail, and I even voted to have them executed. I'd go to their hangouts and try to make them curse Jesus. I was obsessed.

"Then, one day, I was on my way to Damascus, with the official paperwork to keep doing my thing. And boom! A light brighter than the sun just zaps me and my crew. We all hit the deck. Then a voice, in Hebrew, says, 'Saul, Saul, why are you coming for me? You're just hurting yourself.'
"I'm like, 'Who are you, boss?'

"And the voice says, 'I'm Jesus. The one you've been hunting. Now get up. I've got a mission for you. You're going to be my witness and tell everyone what you saw today and what I'm about to show you. I'm sending you to the outsiders to give them a life-changing moment, to show them the difference between dark and light, so they can choose light. To show them the difference between Satan and God, so they can choose God. I'm sending you to tell them their past is cancelled and they're part of the family now.'

"So, King Agrippa, what was I supposed to do? You don't just ghost a vision like that! I was all in. I started telling everyone about this massive life-change, this turn to God, in Damascus, then Jerusalem, and then basically the whole world.

"And that's why the Jews jumped me in the Temple. They want to keep God all to themselves. But God's had my back, and I'm still here, telling everyone, from kings to kids, the same thing. And it's all stuff the prophets and Moses said would happen: the Messiah had to die, and then, with his transformation from the dead, he'd be the first sign of God's new day for everyone, no matter who they are.
Paul pressed on: "King Agrippa, you know all about this stuff—none of it happened in some dark corner. King Agrippa, do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do—I'm sure of it!"
Festus, the governor, totally loses it. "Paul, you're nuts! You've been reading too many books!"

But Paul is chill. "Respectfully, Your Honor, I'm not crazy. I'm telling you the truth. The king knows what's up. This wasn't some secret. King Agrippa, you believe the prophets, right? Rhetorical question. I know you do."
Agrippa's like, "Listen, you keep talking like that and you're gonna make me a Christian."
Paul, still in chains, says, "That's the goal! I'm praying that you and everyone listening today would be just like me... except for these chains, obviously."
Then the king, the governor, and all the other officials get up and leave. They all agree, "This guy's done nothing wrong. He shouldn't be in jail."
And Agrippa tells Festus, "He could've been set free if he hadn't played the 'I appeal to Caesar' card."

title: The Ultimate Storm and a Crazy Shipwreck
paragraphs: §The Shipwreck

Alright, so the second they figured out the travel plans to Italy, they put Paul and some other guys on lockdown with this big shot centurion, Julius. This guy was basically the head of an elite security squad. We all hopped on a ship from Adramyttium that was heading toward Ephesus and other spots out west. Aristarchus, a bro from Thessalonica, came with us.
The next day, we docked at Sidon, and Julius was actually pretty chill with Paul. He let him hop off the boat and hang with his friends for a bit, which was cool.

Back on the water, we had to sail north of Cyprus because the wind was totally against us. After a rough ride, we finally made it to Myra. There, the centurion found an Egyptian ship going to Italy and moved us all over. The weather turned awful again, and we could barely stay on course. It took forever, but we finally got to a place called Good Harbor on the south side of Crete.

We'd ruined a ton of time, and it was already past the fall equinox, which meant sailing was super dangerous. Paul was like, "Hey, hold up. I've got a bad feeling about this. If we sail now, we're gonna wreck the ship, lose all our stuff, and maybe even die. Seriously."

But the captain and the ship's owner said, "Nah, this harbor is terrible for the winter." They totally ghosted Paul's warning and convinced the centurion to risk it for a better spot down the coast called Phoenix.

A little breeze picked up and they said, "See? Perfect sailing weather!" So they took off. Big mistake. Almost immediately, this monster storm, a legit nor'easter, just wrecked them. The ship was getting tossed around like a toy, and they completely lost control.

We barely made it behind a small island called Clauda, where we managed to get the lifeboat secured and lower the sails. We were trying to avoid some rocky areas but couldn't get close, so we just threw out some anchors to slow our drift.

The next day, the storm was still raging, so they started chucking all the cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. Day three, they were still in panic mode and started throwing everything else over the side—all the gear, all the food. Total chaos.
For days, we didn't see the sun or stars. Just non-stop wind and waves pounding the ship. Everyone was pretty sure they were gonna die.

Nobody wanted to eat; everyone was just waiting for the end. Then Paul stands up and is like, "Guys, I told you so back in Crete. We wouldn't be in this mess if you'd listened. But whatever. Good news, though! From now on, things are looking up. I promise not a single one of you will drown. The ship, though? Yeah, the ship's toast."

He went on, "Last night, an angel from the God I serve stood right next to me and said, 'Don't sweat it, Paul. You're gonna meet Caesar, and for your sake, everyone sailing with you is going to live.' So cheer up, my guys! I totally believe God. He's gonna do exactly what he said. But, uh, we're definitely gonna shipwreck on some island."

On the fourteenth night of being tossed around the Adriatic Sea, around midnight, the sailors got a feeling we were close to land. They measured the water depth and it was 120 feet, then 90 feet. Panicking that we were about to crash into rocks, they dropped four anchors and just prayed for morning.

Some of the sailors, the cowards, tried to bail. They lowered the lifeboat, pretending they were just setting more anchors. But Paul saw right through their scam and told the centurion, "If these guys don't stay with the ship, we're all dead." So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and let it float away.

Just before dawn, Paul got everyone together. "We haven't eaten in two weeks! Nobody's felt like it. But you guys need to eat now. You'll need the energy for what's coming. I'm telling you, you'll all get out of this without a scratch."

Then he took some bread, thanked God for it, and passed it around. Everyone—all 276 of us—finally ate something. After the meal, they threw the rest of the grain overboard to make the ship even lighter.

When the sun came up, nobody recognized the place, but they saw a bay with a beach. They decided to try and run the ship aground there. They cut the anchors, untied the rudder, raised a sail, and went for it. But they didn't make it. They hit a reef, and the ship just started to break apart.

The soldiers' first thought was to kill all the prisoners so no one could swim away and escape. But the centurion wanted to save Paul, so he shut that down. He ordered everyone who could swim to jump in and go for the shore, and the rest to grab a piece of the ship and float on it. And just like that, every single person made it to land safely.

title: The One With the Snake and the Sick Dude
paragraphs: §Snake Bite in Malta

So, after that insane shipwreck, we all crawl onto this island, totally drenched and freezing. Turns out we're on Malta, and the locals are super chill. They build this massive bonfire for us, which is clutch because it's pouring rain and we're soaked.

Paul, being the stand-up guy he is, starts helping gather wood. He grabs a bunch of sticks, and as he throws them on the fire, this gnarly snake, woken up by the heat, latches onto his hand. The locals see this and are like, "Whoa, this guy must be a murderer, and that's some serious karma." But Paul just shakes the snake off into the fire like it's no big deal. Everyone's waiting for him to drop dead, but when he doesn't, they totally flip and decide he must be a god or something.

Then we meet this important official named Publius, who's the head honcho of the island. He invites us to his place and treats us like royalty for three days. His dad is super sick with a crazy fever, so Paul goes in, prays for him, and boom—the guy's healed. The news of this transformation spreads like wildfire, and pretty soon, everyone on the island who's sick is lining up to get healed by Paul.

We ended up chilling on Malta for three months. The people there were awesome and hooked us up with everything we needed for the rest of our trip. We hopped on a ship from Egypt that had been docked there for the winter and set sail for Italy. It had this cool Gemini sign on the front.
§Paul in Rome

We made a few stops, and then finally, we got to Rome. Some of our Christian buds heard we were coming and met us on the road. It was a pretty emotional reunion. When we got into the city, the Romans let Paul get his own place, with a soldier to guard him, of course.

Three days later, Paul calls a meeting with the local Jewish leaders. He's like, "Look, guys, I got arrested in Jerusalem on bogus charges. The Romans checked it out and were ready to let me go, but the Jews in Jerusalem threw a fit, so I had to appeal to Caesar. I'm not trying to start beef with our people; I'm here for Israel. I'm a prisoner for hope, not for being a hater."

The leaders said, "We haven't heard anything bad about you, but we've heard this 'Christian' thing is super unpopular. We're down to hear what you have to say." So they set a date, and a bunch of them came over to Paul's place. He talked to them all day, from morning 'til night, telling them all about God's kingdom and trying to get them on board with Jesus, using the scriptures to back it up.

Some of them were convinced, but others just weren't having it. When the haters started arguing, Paul was like, "Alright, one last thing. The Holy Spirit was totally right when he told our ancestors through Isaiah: 'You'll listen, but you won't get it. You'll look, but you won't see. These people are clueless.' So, you had your chance. Now I'm taking this message to the non-Jews, and trust me, they're gonna be all over it."
Paul stayed in his rented house for two whole years, and his door was always open. He told everyone who came to visit about God's kingdom and Jesus, and nobody tried to shut him down.
